newsitem.title: ESTONIA: TALLINNA TO LESSEN ACTIVITY IN OVERNIGHT MARKET.
newsitem.headline: TALLINNA TO LESSEN ACTIVITY IN OVERNIGHT MARKET.

text.p: Tallinna Bank said on Friday it will decrease its activity in the local overnight market because of the instability and illiquidity it has witnessed lately.
"We will probably decrease our activity...and use more foreign credits," Martti Siimann, the bank's financial markets head, told a news conference.
Tallinna Bank said it had to borrow money at an exorbitant rate from the local overnight market on Tuesday to meet the central bank's minimum reserve requirements.
It borrowed 3.6 million kroons from Hansabank at the rate of 10.25 percent, about six basis points above the average.
Siimann said that other banks also borrowed money in the overnight market at a considerably higher rate.
"The relation between demand and supply was out of balance... with much demand and only one offer," Siimann said.
Hansabank interest rate products and financial risks department head Erkki Raasuke told Reuters that the interest went up steadily on Tuesday from four percent to 10.25 percent.
Tallinna Bank's director of credits and corporate banking, Indrek Pajumaa, said that this was the first warning signal of the illiquid situation in Estonia's overnight market.
Erkki Raasuke of Hansabank said banks have proposed to the central bank to start releasing the online situation of the overnight market.
"It would help a lot when banks know how much free money is in the market," he added.
Raasuke said the interest rates in the overnight market are expected to come fall from this week's 5.43 percent.
"Deals have been made at a reasonable level from today," Raasuke said.
